questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: As I'm dyslexic it was important for me to choose a university which would provide similar assistance to that of UCPH. I knew I wanted to study outside of Europe to experience a new culture and possibly travel during the semester. Choosing an english-speaking country was also important to me, to allow easier communication with local students.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The university was great at providing the necessary information. An introduction lecture was given the first day and during orientation week a lot of information is provided, so try to come if possible.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The university provides a shuttle service from the airport to your accommodation. That was really helpfull after such a long journey. They also send out several emails with the schedule for the orientation week so browse through and see what you want to join.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Stop 1 is really helpfull. It is located on campus and is open every day. You don't need to book an appointment, but it is the best place to have any question answered.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I chose Unilodge Carlton which is a student accommodation located 5 min walk from campus. The location was really great and the staff very nice, however I would not chose this again. The kitchen was way too small for the amount of students and the interior of my room was a hotel, meaning no closet space, desk or anything.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
When choosing student accommodation off campus please look at the dates. Most want the rooms rented out for an entire semester (until january), the the options for a flexible stay is limited. Everything is really expensive, so I would recommend leaving with house mates off campus or maybe try a different Unilodge. Prior to arrival you could look at the Facebook page Fairy Floss Real Estate,
flatmatefinders.com.au
or
flatmates.com.au
to see if you could find a furnished place.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The handbook is easy to use once you get to know it. Most courses are available to exchange students, and each course has a large description of assessment, important dates and how to enroll.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: First you register/apply for a number of courses. You normally will register for more than you need to be a full time student. After the university has approved your choices they will open for enrollment. Some courses might be full at first, but as students needs to create their own timetable spots may become available if others choice to drop the class. So keep an eye out during the enrollment days.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The university sends out an email describing how to enroll in each subject, and how many you should apply for. They will assess each course you apply for in terms of you meeting any criteria, but also all of your subjects together. I got a course of pharmacology rejected because the institute though it was better for me to focus on another pharmacology course. They felt both courses might be too much to take on.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted. As mentioned one class was rejected, but I has only chosen to register for this as a backup.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Pick from interest. Only take classes that you are interested in and maybe try something completely new. I chose to have 2 more easy courses in terms of assessment, and this was a nice balance.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took a single first year class, two second year classes and one third year class. All of the classes were not too difficult, and reading was not required to understand the material.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Lectures are like UCPH, but can be streamed if preferred. During the semester be prepared for quizzes and tests that count in your final grade. The quizzes, midsemester test and final examination are all closed book, and in addition focuses on more smaller details like names of proteins or processes rather than the overall understanding like on UCPH

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Our Planet, Our Health (UNIB10017)
Australia in the Wine World (AGRI10039)
Pharmacology: How Drugs Work (PHRM20001)
Stem Cells in Development & Regeneration (CEDB30004)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend them all except (UNIB10017). This was just really weird structured, not very interesting and very easy.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Due to where I lived I had to spend some money decorating the place. It was just not furnished for a longterm student to live there. I spend about 4000 DKK getting stuff for the kitchen and my room.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Overall public transportation was a lot cheaper and easier to use than I had expected, so that was a nice surprise. It was very easy to take public transportation to different national parks in the area around Melbourne.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Unimelb has a wide variety of societies and clubs. I joined Musex which is a society for exchange students. They host a few parties throughout the semester, and other events. 
I also joined Swifties society as well as Drawing and painting club. Signing up to clubs costs 5 dollars, and the events can cost an additional few dollars.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend all the clubs that I joined, and just joining something in general. They host really nice events and it is a great place to meet other students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: In Melbourne I would recommed simply getting to know the local area fast. There are plenty of places to see, and time goes by really fast. Go see an AFL game and visit many of the markets in the city. A short drive from Melbourne is Great Ocean Road, Philip Island and Wilsons Promonotory which is also worth seeing. Just travel as much as possible. We went to Tasmania on an extended weekend (6 days) and would highly recommed going.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was really easy to adjust. People are very nice and helpfull in addition the city is very liveable.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to events in the beginning and sign up for sports or societies.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: No major differences. Be aware that a lot of the bars and clubs close at 1 am, so choice wisely when going out.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Overall the culture is much like in Denmark and other places in Europe. Australians are super friendly and talkative, so don't hesitate to ask anything.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be prepared to spend a lot of money on travelling. You will have plenty of time to travel during the semester and after the semester. So take every opportunity, and explore as much of Australia as possible. 
Bring warm clothe as it is cold in the beginning. No need to bring a big jacket, but a few sweaters is a good idea.
Embrace the Australian way of life which is much more laid back.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You can get good grades with way less effort, but make sure you do all the quizzes during the semester.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Learning a different approach to studying, and also learning to be on your own so far away from home. You will settle into a rhythm really fast, so just remember to enjoy it while it lasts.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being away from friends and family with the large time difference.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
